newsitem.title: EGYPT: Turkey's Erbakan in Egypt ahead of Libya visit.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Erbakan in Egypt ahead of Libya visit.

text.p: Turkish Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan arrived in Cairo on Wednesday for a two-day visit ahead of a controversial trip to Libya.
Erbakan is scheduled to meet his Egyptian counterpart Kamal el-Ganzouri and President Hosni Mubarak on Thursday. On Friday, he will leave for Tripoli to boost trade ties.
Turkish trade officials have already arrived in Tripoli to seek Libya's payment of outstanding debts of up to $365 million due to Turkish building contractors.
The Turkish prime minister's trip has renewed concern that he aims to divert Turkey away from the West.
His coalition partner, Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller, said the visit was ill-timed and a leading figure from her party has threatened to resign over the trip.
The United States, a close Turkish ally which says Libya sponsors terrorism, has said it was concerned about the trip.
But the Islamist Erbakan told reporters in Ankara he only hoped to strengthen commercial relations with Libya.
"This visit is not aimed against any country or society in the world," he said. "America is our friend and ally."
In addition to Libya and Egypt, Erbakan will also visit Nigeria, itself something of an international outcast for its human rights record and lack of democracy.
